Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

The test `['org.apache.commons.math3.linear.RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest.testFullRank()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
50 :     @Test
51 :     public void testFullRank() {
52 : 
53 :         RealMatrix base = MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix(new double[][] {
54 :             { 0.1159548705,      0.,           0.,           0.      },
55 :             { 0.0896442724, 0.1223540781,      0.,           0.      },
56 :             { 0.0852155322, 4.558668e-3,  0.1083577299,      0.      },
57 :             { 0.0905486674, 0.0213768077, 0.0128878333, 0.1014155693 }
58 :         });
59 :

61 :

64 :

66 :         RealMatrix rebuiltM = root.multiply(root.transpose());
67 :         Assert.assertEquals(0.0, m.subtract(rebuiltM).getNorm(), 1.0e-15);
68 : 
69 :         // the pivoted Cholesky decomposition is *not* unique. Here, the root is
70 :         // not equal to the original trianbular base matrix
71 :         Assert.assertTrue(root.subtract(base).getNorm() > 0.3); // error occurred here
72 : 
73 :     }
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
junit.framework.AssertionFailedError
	at org.junit.Assert.fail(Assert.java:86)
	at org.junit.Assert.assertTrue(Assert.java:41)
	at org.junit.Assert.assertTrue(Assert.java:52)
	at org.apache.commons.math3.linear.RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest.testFullRank(RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest.java:71)
```

Title: Diagnosis of test `testFullRank` failure in `RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest`

Details: The failing test `testFullRank` in class `RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest` checks the Cholesky decomposition of a positive matrix `m` derived from a base matrix multiplied by its transpose. The test asserts that the decomposition produces a root matrix that reproduces `m` almost exactly (within a very small tolerance), and also that the root matrix differs significantly from the original base matrix by a norm difference of more than 0.3.

The failure occurs on the second assertion at line 71:
```java
Assert.assertTrue(root.subtract(base).getNorm() > 0.3);
```
This assertion expects the norm difference between `root` and `base` to be greater than 0.3. The failure implies the norm difference is not large enough, i.e., the root matrix is closer to the base matrix than expected.

This indicates that the pivoted Cholesky decomposition—which is not unique and often produces a root matrix different from the base triangular matrix—is producing a root matrix closely resembling the base matrix in this case, contrary to the test's expectation.

The relevant tested class is `RectangularCholeskyDecomposition`, with constructor:
```java
.RectangularCholeskyDecomposition(org.apache.commons.math3.linear.RealMatrix, double)
```
and method:
```java
.getRootMatrix()
```
These provide the root matrix used in the test.

To understand why the root matrix is not differing sufficiently from the base matrix, the implementation of these two methods should be examined to see how the decomposition and storage/retrieval of the root matrix is done and why it may be closer to the base matrix than expected.

Next, I will review the constructor implementation of `RectangularCholeskyDecomposition.RealMatrix` with a double argument.
